sections.title: Take the first steps
sections.blurb: Define a job, start it, and read back what it did. Start at the top.

sections.title: Start jobs
sections.blurb: Every way to start work: now, later, once only, by name, or many at a time.

sections.title: Run work on a schedule
sections.blurb: Recurring work as one permanent job: by cron, by interval, in a time zone, or from a calendar.

sections.title: Keep another system in sync
sections.blurb: One job that keeps calling a service and remembers how far it got.

sections.title: Make work survive a crash
sections.blurb: Steps and variables record what a handler finished, so a retry or a restart carries on instead of starting over.

sections.title: Wait for people, events, and time
sections.blurb: A waiting job is a row. No worker and no process stays busy while it waits.

sections.title: Split work across child jobs
sections.blurb: Fan out, join the results, and decide what a failed child means.

sections.title: Decide what happens when work fails
sections.blurb: Retries, backoff, timeouts, deadlines, and ending a job on purpose.

sections.title: Control order and load
sections.blurb: Keep jobs that touch the same thing from running over each other.

more.text: See order, limits, and pacing move in the interactive explainer

sections.title: Watch and control running work
sections.blurb: Read what happened, find jobs, and cancel, pause, resume, or restart them.

sections.title: Get told when something breaks
sections.blurb: Alerts raised by failures or by your own code, routed where your team looks.

sections.title: Test without sleeps or polling
sections.blurb: The real runtime on a throwaway database, driven one tick at a time.

sections.title: Deploy and scale
sections.blurb: Split the API from the worker, add workers, and tune them.

more.text: See workers share work and recover it in the interactive explainer
